PullRequest.Title: agent Host: Reduce redundant Git work in AH sessions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Reduce Git overhead in Agent Host session preparation and checkpoint capture, particularly on Windows:

- **Skip unnecessary reviewed-ref deletion.** Enumerate existing refs and avoid deletion when none match. Add an optional strict lookup mode to distinguish an empty result from a failed lookup, preserving known-ref cleanup when enumeration fails.
- **Read branches concurrently.** Resolve the current and default branches in parallel after repository and HEAD validation, retaining existing fallbacks and retry behavior.
- **Deduplicate checkpoint captures by checkout root.** Process each checkout once per successful baseline, turn-start, or turn-end capture. Preserve retries after failures, fresh snapshots on later turns, and separate linked worktrees.

Adds regression coverage for concurrency, ref enumeration, duplicate captures, and failure recovery.

No changes to session identity, provider-startup ordering, checkpoint-before-mutation guarantees.

## Performance evidence
| Change in this PR | Performance evidence | Measurement scope |
|---|---|---|
| Skip reviewed-ref deletion when no refs exist | Windows: **222 → 174 ms**, saving **~49 ms** | Awaited idle-draft disposal, not total first-progress time |
| Read current and default branches concurrently | Windows: **182 → 139 ms**, saving **~43 ms** | Branch discovery; real-host runs also showed **~40–50 ms** less affected new-session preparation |
| Deduplicate checkpoint captures by checkout root | **63–399 ms saved on Windows**, **7–48 ms on Linux** | Turn-start checkpoint capture with an existing baseline, for multiple folders sharing one checkout |
| Same checkpoint deduplication change, measured through the real host | **1.7–2.1 s faster** new-session progress; **1.6–1.9 s faster** follow-ups | Send-to-first-meaningful protocol progress with three folders sharing one dirty checkout; new sessions run on a warm host |

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostCheckpointService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostReviewService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\shared\worktreeIsolation.test.ts` — **98 tests passed**.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Real-Git Windows/Linux probes verified captured trees, unchanged real indexes, and separate linked-worktree captures.
- Regression negative control confirmed that the original implementation fails the new duplicate-capture test.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Multi-root checkpoint loops repeated full Git working-tree capture and commit/ref work for every configured folder even when several folders shared one checkout root.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Turn-start and turn-end checkpoint latency scaled with folder count rather than unique repositories, adding repeated Git subprocess and filesystem work for common multi-folder sessions.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Successful baseline, turn-start, and turn-end captures now mark the resolved repository root complete and skip additional folders resolving to that same root, reducing expensive working-tree snapshots and commit/ref subprocesses from O(folders) to O(unique checkout roots) per capture phase.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base implementation iterated every configured working directory and invoked _writeCheckpointCommit for each. That helper calls captureWorkingTreeAsTree, which runs git status/rev-parse/index discovery and may create a temp index and run additional Git commands. Multiple workspace folders can resolve to the same checkout root; the added ResourceSet guard at RIGHT:75 makes each successful repository capture occur once per phase while the new tests prove retries remain possible after failure and later turns still take fresh snapshots.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Two independent Git branch-discovery subprocess chains were serialized on the session configuration critical path.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening or resolving Agent Host session configuration incurred additive current/default branch discovery latency, especially on Windows where Git process startup is material.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Current-branch and default-branch discovery now overlap, so session configuration waits for the slower independent Git read rather than their sum, without increasing request cardinality.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base lines awaited getCurrentBranch before starting getDefaultBranch. Both methods execute independent read-only Git subprocesses, and resolveIsolationConfig awaits _getGitInfo on the session-configuration critical path. RIGHT:1557 starts both reads together after repository and HEAD validation, while _pendingGitInfo continues coalescing overlapping callers for one working directory.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Session cleanup unconditionally spawned a Git update-ref subprocess for known ref names, including repositories with no matching reviewed refs and repeated folders sharing a checkout.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Awaited session-data disposal accumulated avoidable Git process startup latency per configured working directory, including the common no-reviewed-ref case.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Successful ref enumeration now filters cleanup to refs that actually exist and avoids spawning git update-ref for empty results; after one folder removes shared-checkout refs, later folders also observe an empty result and skip redundant deletion.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base implementation always passed the non-empty known-ref set to deleteRefs after enumeration. deleteRefs launches `git update-ref --stdin -z` even when those refs do not exist, so session disposal paid one process per working directory and repeated it for multiple folders in the same checkout. The changed strict enumeration computes only existing refs and RIGHT:310 skips deleteRefs when none remain; failure/unavailable enumeration retains the previous known-ref fallback.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve Agent Host session configuration for a Git-backed working directory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider config resolution awaits resolveIsolationConfig, which awaits repository discovery, HEAD validation, and branch discovery before the session configuration can be returned. The changed current/default branch reads are therefore on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover repository root with Git when the repository-root LRU is cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one discovery sequence for the request URI, coalesced for overlapping cold callers; zero discovery subprocesses on an LRU hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same repository discovery and cache behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks HEAD and branch discovery on cold cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per fresh configuration read for a Git repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks branch reads and correctly avoids them for an unborn repository.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read current branch and remote default branch through independent Git command chains.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One current-branch chain and one default-branch chain per fresh read; effective aggregate concurrency is two, with no collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commands ran sequentially, current branch first and default branch second.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both results are required, but the changed code waits for their maximum duration rather than their sum.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One primary working directory per configuration request. Overlapping requests for the same URI are coalesced by _pendingGitInfo; fresh requests intentionally reread Git state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository-root and HEAD checks remain sequential prerequisites. After HEAD validation, getCurrentBranch and getDefaultBranch run with effective concurrency 2. getCurrentBranch internally runs one Git command normally and a second only for detached HEAD; getDefaultBranch runs one command normally and up to two additional sequential verification commands when origin/HEAD exists. There is no cross-repository fan-out in this scenario.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getRepositoryRoot uses a 100-entry LRU and a per-key sequencer, so warm requests avoid repository discovery work. Branch state is deliberately not retained after a request; only overlapping callers share the in-flight read. There is no negative branch cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path, subprocess implementations, coalescing map, and Promise.all scheduling are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact savings depend on OS Git process startup and whether origin/HEAD needs verification. Aggregate concurrency remains bounded at two read-only processes for one repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes serialized boundary latency without increasing command count or creating unbounded concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Capture baseline, turn-start, and turn-end checkpoints for a multi-folder Agent Host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Baseline capture is started best-effort after provider materialization and is off the immediate materialize path. Turn-start capture begins alongside provider selection round trips but is awaited before the prompt is sent, so any remaining snapshot work can block first provider progress. Turn-end capture is not awaited by later contributions, but Git-backed changeset refresh is chained after it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each working directory to a repository root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F service calls per phase; cold Git discovery only for cache misses, with subsequent paths served from the repository-root LRU.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequential prefix of each folder iteration; turn-start instances can affect prompt dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture a working tree using status, rev-parse/index discovery, and when dirty temp-index staging/write-tree commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After this diff, U successful captures per phase rather than F when folders share roots; failures can retry on a later folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The operation was repeated for every folder even when several folders resolved to the same checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dominant checkpoint cost; turn-start capture is awaited before provider send, baseline is off the immediate path, and turn-end gates only the subsequent Git-backed refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/copy/delete a temporary index directory and restage changed paths for dirty repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per unique successful repository capture that cannot use the clean-tree fast path; retries occur only after failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Could be repeated per folder sharing a checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the same snapshot boundary and can block turn-start provider dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create checkpoint commits, resolve parent/baseline refs, and update checkpoint refs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Successful work scales with U per phase after deduplication; turn end performs parent/ref reads and two commit-tree operations plus one update-ref per unique root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Commit/ref work could repeat for all F folders sharing a checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Baseline and turn-end placement are mostly off immediate interaction progress; turn-start baseline establishment can remain on prompt dispatch when a baseline is absent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/read turn records and persist the chosen checkpoint ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Constant per turn, not per folder; the repository loop does not amplify database writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Turn-start record work is awaited before provider send; turn-end persistence gates only checkpoint completion and subsequent refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F configured working directories resolving to U unique checkout roots, where U <= F. Multiple workspace folders commonly share one checkout; linked worktrees intentionally count as distinct roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Checkpoint operations are serialized per session by SequencerByKey and iterate directories sequentially. Inside each working-tree capture, status, HEAD tree, and index-path reads run concurrently. The diff does not add repository-level parallelism; it reduces successful full captures from F to U per phase. A failed attempt remains eligible for retry through a later folder.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository-root discovery is backed by the Git service's 100-entry LRU, so repeated nested folders can be warm after first discovery, though one lookup is still issued per configured folder. No working-tree snapshot is cached across phases or turns; fresh snapshots are intentionally taken. Completed-root sets live only for one operation, so they cannot retain repositories or suppress later captures.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added operation-local ResourceSet guards all three loops, success marking and failure retries are explicit, and tests establish F-to-U capture reduction while preserving fresh later snapshots and linked-worktree separation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Savings depend on how often sessions configure multiple folders in one checkout, repository size/dirty state, and warm repository-root caches. The mechanism and reduced full-capture cardinality are not uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes repeated Git and filesystem work while preserving retry, lifecycle, and fresh-snapshot behavior. A validated prior repeated-work regression was recorded internally.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose session review refs across configured working directories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: onWillDeleteSessionData registers disposal with waitUntil, so enumeration and any deletion must settle before session data deletion can finish. The directories are processed sequentially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each working directory to its repository root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F service calls, with Git subprocesses only on repository-root cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequential and awaited by session-data deletion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate reviewed refs with git for-each-ref in strict error mode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per configured working directory; the glob is scoped to the sanitized session prefix and results are filtered before deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One best-effort enumeration per working directory with a slightly narrower glob that omitted the direct session ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited cleanup work. Strict mode changes error distinction, not normal command cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Batch-delete existing reviewed refs with git update-ref --stdin -z.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when enumeration finds no existing relevant refs; otherwise one process for all matching refs. For duplicate folders in one checkout, normally only the first deletion runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One update-ref process was launched per working directory because the known-ref set was always non-empty, even when no refs existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by session-data deletion, but the diff removes no-op and repeated invocations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F working directories and R distinct repositories, plus the number of reviewed refs matching one sanitized session prefix. Multiple folders may resolve to the same checkout.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One directory is processed at a time. Each successful enumeration is followed by at most one batched update-ref subprocess if matching refs exist. There is no burst; deleteRefs batches all refs for that directory into one process.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository roots use the Git service LRU. Ref existence is intentionally read fresh; after the first folder deletes refs in a shared repository, a later folder enumerates an empty result and now skips deletion. Failed enumeration falls back to known refs rather than caching a failure.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listRefNamesWithOids and deleteRefs each map directly to one Git child process, and the changed empty-result guard is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact disposal saving depends on folder count and existing review refs. Prefix collisions could enlarge enumeration output only for sessions whose sanitized IDs are prefixes of others, but filtering is linear and this does not establish a realistic regression against the removed update-ref processes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff replaces unconditional deletion with fresh existence filtering and preserves cleanup fallback on enumeration failure. A validated prior boundary-fanout regression was recorded internally.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff pages. No actionable performance regression was introduced. The PR instead fixes three concrete mechanisms: repeated checkpoint capture per folder sharing a checkout, serialized branch discovery on configuration resolution, and unconditional reviewed-ref deletion subprocesses.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
